relationship_to_at_m1_registry: at-capability-state-registry.json is the AT-M1 BASELINE measurement, pinned to canonical main fa5e5c4. It is not a live dashboard and AT-M2 does not edit it: rewriting a baseline would destroy the only record of what the platform looked like before this milestone.

This file records the DELTA AT-M2 produced, against that baseline, using the same six allowed states and the same rule that a capability is classified by repository evidence rather than by the existence of a name.

capabilities.evidence: migrations/036 creates actor_principals (principal_type/display_name/status) and agent_profiles (principal_id, agent_key, role, capabilities, transport_stream, tool_policy_profile, model_provider_ref). TeamStore.register_agent mints one runtime_agent principal per agent, idempotently by agent_key. Distinct from the task/authorization Actor.principal_id, which is untouched.

project_team_memberships with membership_state invited|active|paused|left and historical left_at. TeamService.form_team recruits a team for a project and is exercised end-to-end by tests/test_at_m2_team_core_demo.py. There is deliberately no separate teams table: a team IS its memberships, as the AT-M1 contract defines it.

team_messages carries recipient_principal_id / recipient_role / recipient_team with a DB CHECK that at least one is set, plus parent_message_id threading. StreamAgent.resolve_publish_target consults the router instead of output_stream whenever a team context is present, and publishes to the team blocked stream rather than falling back when nobody is eligible.

shared/sdk/agent_team/router.py selects a successor from declared capabilities and current membership, records the eligible set with per-candidate rejection reasons, and refuses production-effect capabilities to the human approval boundary. Withdrawing a capability or a member changes the decision with no operator input (tests/test_at_m2_team_core.py).

agent_handoffs exists with from/to principal, reason, context_refs and state offered|accepted|declined|withdrawn|expired; ownership moves only on accept (TeamStore.accept_handoff). PARTIAL rather than IMPLEMENTED: no runtime agent offers a handoff on the autonomous path yet -- routing, not handoff, moves work in AT-M2.

team_decisions now exists with options_considered, selected_option, rationale_summary and dissent_summary, kept free-form so it can never carry a Review Gate Action (INV-03). Still PARTIAL: no runtime agent records one, because that needs proposals AT-M2 does not generate.

conversation_threads plus team_messages give the team a durable project-scoped record with audit refs. Still PARTIAL: the context is persisted and readable but nothing reasons over it, and there is still no cross-project context.

The orchestrator graph is no longer linear: audit -> route_next -> {dispatch | team_blocked} is a real conditional edge decided at runtime from team capability. PARTIAL and not IMPLEMENTED: this is conditional ROUTING, not replanning -- there is no PlanRevision, no back-edge and no plan to revise. AT-M3/AT-M4 own that.

UNCHANGED by AT-M2. shared/sdk/agent_discussion remains a deterministic template fixture. Team messages are addressed and durable but their content is composed by the sending agent, not reasoned: AT-M2 deliberately excludes LLM-authored content.

UNCHANGED by AT-M2. No LLM provider, planner or network call is added; the router is capability matching, not reasoning. Recorded here only so a reader cannot infer that runtime teams implied runtime reasoning.
